newsitem.title: ITALY: Lower inflation raises Italy rate cut hopes - Treu.
newsitem.headline: Lower inflation raises Italy rate cut hopes - Treu.

text.p: Falling inflation in August has raised hopes about the prospect of a cut in official interest rates, Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said on Tuesday.

"It has been a reasonably quiet summer. The fact that inflation has fallen is positive and raises optimism about the chances of an interest rate cut," he told reporters before a meeting with Prime Minister Romano Prodi.
Preliminary data for August pointed to inflation falling to 3.3-3.4 percent year-on-year from 3.6 percent in July.
Treu added he hoped threatened strike action by the major metal workers' unions could be averted. Metal workers and employers are locked in disagreement over renewal of labour contracts.
Unions are demanding full compensation for higher-than- forecast inflation in the 1994-95 period.
"I don't think there is any reason to be alarmist over the outlook for the autumn," Treu said.
The Italian cabinet meets on Wednesday for the first time after the summer recess. The 1997 budget is not on the official agenda but the package will be discussed, officials said.
